subject.title: fix: allow macOS gateway restart while LaunchAgent owns its port

question: Should a macOS LaunchAgent restart proceed through `kickstart -k` for every busy port, or only when the listener is verified as the managed OpenClaw gateway while preserving a safe failure for unrelated owners?
rationale: The PR intentionally leaves direct-caller readiness outside the service contract, so choosing between listener classification and a broader restart/readiness contract is a product and lifecycle-semantics decision rather than a mechanical test repair.

options.title: Classify the busy listener before restart
options.body: Allow the managed LaunchAgent listener case to reach `kickstart -k`, but preserve a clear failure when the port is held by an unrelated process.

options.title: Broaden the restart contract
options.body: Make the service-level restart operation confirm replacement health for direct callers, then permit launchd to attempt replacement even when the listener identity is not known.

options.title: Pause this narrow removal
options.body: Retain the existing precondition until the desired direct-caller and unrelated-port behavior is explicitly agreed.

recommendation.title: Classify the busy listener before restart
recommendation.body: Allow the managed LaunchAgent listener case to reach `kickstart -k`, but preserve a clear failure when the port is held by an unrelated process.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged LaunchAgent stop-path change is the closest current-main ownership signal for the lifecycle boundary at issue.
